name: Morning Tile
tagline: She checks in for herself, because that's the door the grandchildren's voices come through.
old_product: The fridge calendar and the daily 'just checking you're alive' call to an ageing parent
fresh_spin: The parent sends the signal instead of being watched: each morning she slides a tile and presses its number on any phone, and that unlocks today's voice note from the family.
boring_but: Boring on the surface, it's a fridge calendar and a phone number. But the check-in is something she does for herself, because it's the door the grandchildren's voices come through.
borrows_from: #20 Facing Out: her signs face out only to the people she chooses, as scarce graded clues (fine / out / call me)
#38 Tally: a check that proves the chain works, with silence escalating only to her one chosen person
summary: Morning Tile is a $12/month family service with a free printed magnetic board on annual plans. Each morning the parent slides a tile (fine, out, call me) and presses its number from any landline or mobile. The IVR logs it, plays today's screened voice note from the family, and sends her reply back to them. The payer sees only the tile and time. Silence past her chosen hour goes to one chosen person, never an alarm at her. Contributors are invited by the payer, OTP-verified, recorded in-app only and approved by the parent. Money or urgency messages are held for review, and the service never calls her.
first_buyer: An adult child (often a woman aged 45-64) who already worries about a parent living alone, the week after a call went unanswered for three hours, and who finds a pendant too much and a daily call too much like inspecting.
why_now: 63M US family caregivers spend about $7,200/yr out of pocket (AARP 2025), and 75% of over-50s want to age in place (AARP 2024). Amazon's $19.99/month Alexa Together is no longer available (Amazon note, May 21, 2025), leaving paying families without a service. Cheap IVR and app infrastructure means no hardware or certification is needed to start.
competitors: Snug Safety: app daily check-in, free; Dispatch plan $19.99/month or $199.99/year
AllsOK, OneTap Safe, KinStatus, Are You Ok?: smartphone check-in apps, free trial then subscription
County and police RUOK daily reassurance calls: free, institution-initiated
Medical alert pendants (Medical Guardian, Lively): about $25-45/month
Alexa Emergency Assist: Amazon's suggested replacement for Alexa Together (pricing unverified)
GrandPad tablets and passive sensors such as Alarm.com Wellness: pricing unverified
price_and_margin: $12/month, or $120/year with the board free. Cost to serve about $1.50/month (IVR at about $0.02 a call, SMS, storage), plus about $3 printed board and shipping, so about $10.50/month contribution. Assumed CAC about $80; at 5% monthly churn, lifetime contribution about $210 (about 2.6x CAC).
channel: First 100: about 30 from the pre-sale demand test, then caregiver Facebook groups, AgingCare forums and sibling referrals ($12 credit). First 1,000: Meta ads to women aged 45-64 with the five-second demo (tile, phone, grandchild's voice, daughter's phone lights up), about $80k of ads over 12 months.
demand_test: Three weeks, about $1.5k: Meta ads ('Mum checks in, and gets a message from the grandkids') to a $12/month card-on-file pre-sale. Go if paid CAC is $60 or less, and in the first 30 families, 70%+ of parents call 5 of 7 days in week 3, with 60%+ of days carrying a family message.
mvp_90_days: Weeks 1-3: demand test with a hand-run IVR. Weeks 4-8: production IVR (Twilio), family app for verified in-app voice notes, parent approval on the line, money and urgency transcript screening, payer dashboard and escalation SMS, printed magnetic boards. Weeks 9-13: onboard 100 families.
kill_metric: Fewer than 60% of parents calling 5 of 7 days by day 60; monthly churn above 8% by month 4; or blended CAC above $100 after month 3.
risks: Grandparent and voice-clone scams: mitigated by verified in-app contributors, parent approval, money screening and no outbound calls
Retention depends on family recording effort; when it stops, the product becomes a commodity check-in
Two people to win (payer and parent) pushes CAC above DTC benchmarks
Free alternatives (Snug free tier, county RUOK calls) cap pricing
Liability if treated as an emergency service; 'not an emergency service' messaging is mandatory
Voice data of family members, including children, must be minimised and secured
three_year: 15-25k families and $2-3.5M ARR. A mains-powered cellular tile slot for parents who'd skip the phone step; an annual 'year of mornings' printed book of approved replies at $49 as a repeat gift; home-care agencies and Medicare Advantage loneliness benefits reselling it, using two years of retention data. No sensors, ever.
best_line: The tile becomes an answering machine that only plays when she says she's fine.

app_version.summary: Morning Tile as a second front door on the same backend, not a separate product. The parent taps a three-tile home-screen widget (fine / out / call me); the tap plays today's screened family voice note, and Reply opens the app to record an answer or photo. The family app shows a daily Live Activity and her reply thread. Silence past her chosen hour goes to her one chosen person, softened (never raised) by an opt-in HealthKit/Health Connect step count. The printed card with the IVR number ships to every family as the always-working fallback.
app_version.parent_flow: Each morning she taps a tile on an iOS 17+ or Android interactive widget, with no app to open and no login; an audio-playback intent plays today's note in place, and Reply opens the app to record. At her chosen hour one notification ('Lily left you something') is her only nudge. Siri App Shortcuts ('Green in Morning Tile') are a bonus. No Watch in v1: a complication only opens the app (two taps), and wearables lag among older adults. If she prefers, or the widget breaks, she presses her tile number on the landline as before.
app_version.family_flow: Siblings on iOS get a Live Activity push-started at her chosen hour (iOS 17.2+) showing 'Mum: green, 8:12', ended once the tile lands, since an activity updates for at most 8 hours and leaves the lock screen by hour 12; broadcast push (iOS 18) is used but saves nothing at family scale. Android siblings get a plain notification. Contributors stay payer-invited, OTP-verified, parent-approved and money-screened. If no tile arrives 90 minutes after her hour, her one chosen person gets 'No tile from Mum yet', shown grey ('up and about') if she opted in and has 300+ steps since 6am; only that boolean leaves her phone.
app_version.vs_board: Lost: an object in her kitchen beside the kettle, the over-80s and the 21% of over-65s without a smartphone, and a check-in that survives a new phone. Gained: no hardware or IVR minutes, photo replies, App Store and web-funnel distribution, and a lock-screen artifact for the family. The new failure is silent: a deleted widget, a replaced phone or muted notifications produce false 'no tile' alerts, which cost the payer's trust faster than churn, so the printed number stays as the fallback. App-only, it competes directly with free Snug and the family WhatsApp group; the only new thing is the gate (the note plays when she says she's fine).
app_version.price: $12/month or $99/year charged to the payer through a hard-paywalled web funnel with in-app purchase alongside; the parent's side is free. Cost to serve under $0.50/month (push, storage, transcript screening), plus 15% on in-app sales. Meta CAC assumed about $70 because two people must still be won; no App Store retention data by age group was found, so retention is the open number.
app_version.verdict: Beside the board, never instead of it. One backend; at setup the payer picks the parent's door (widget, phone number or both) and every family gets the printed card with the number. The family app is needed either way, and the parent widget adds about three weeks to it, so it ships inside the same 90 days. Kill the widget door if under 60% of app parents tap 5 of 7 days by day 60. App alone scores 3/8/5: Snug plus a gated voice note, no new dated trigger, and it loses the parents over 80 who most need it; bundled with the line, market fit stays at 6.
